title: Ζεὺς καὶ ἀλώπηξ
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 119 (= Perry 107). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ζεὺς ἀγασάμενος ἀλώπεκος τὸ συνετὸν τῶν φρενῶν καὶ τὸ ποικίλον τὸ βασίλειον αὐτῇ τῶν ἀλόγων ζῴων ἐνεχείρισε.
sentences.tr: Zeus agasamenos alōpekos to syneton tōn phrenōn kai to poikilon to basileion autēi tōn alogōn zōiōn enecheirise.
sentences.l: Zeus, having admired the shrewdness of the fox's wits and her dappled cunning, put into her hands the kingship of the animals that have no reason.
sentences.n: τὸ συνετόν and τὸ ποικίλον are neuter adjectives made into abstract nouns by the article — the shrewd thing about her wits, the many-coloured thing about her; ποικίλος is of dappled skins and embroidered cloth before it is of a mind. τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα is the standing Greek phrase for animals as creatures without reason or speech, set against man. ἐγχειρίζω is literally to put a thing into someone's hand.

sentences.t: Βουλόμενος δὲ γνῶναι εἰ τὴν τύχην μεταλλάξασα μετεβάλετο καὶ τὴν γλισχρότητα, φερομένης αὐτῆς ἐν φορείῳ κάνθαρον παρὰ τὴν ὄψιν ἀφῆκεν.
sentences.tr: Boulomenos de gnōnai ei tēn tychēn metallaxasa metebaleto kai tēn glischrotēta, pheromenēs autēs en phoreiōi kantharon para tēn opsin aphēken.
sentences.l: But wishing to know whether, having exchanged her fortune, she had changed her grasping temper as well, while she was being carried in a litter he let a beetle loose past her eyes.
sentences.n: φερομένης αὐτῆς ἐν φορείῳ is a genitive absolute — a noun and participle standing outside the grammar of the main clause to set the scene; the fables run on them, and this batch is full of them. γλισχρότης, from γλίσχρος 'sticky', is the clutching, grasping temper that will not let a thing go by. The φορεῖον is the litter carried on men's shoulders, the conveyance of high rank: the fox is travelling as a queen.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ ἀντισχεῖν μὴ δυναμένη, ἐπειδὴ περιίπτατο τῷ φορείῳ, ἀναπηδήσασα ἀκόσμως συλλαβεῖν αὐτὸν ἐπειρᾶτο.
sentences.tr: Hē de antischein mē dynamenē, epeidē periiptato tōi phoreiōi, anapēdēsasa akosmōs syllabein auton epeirato.
sentences.l: But she, not being able to hold out, when it flew round about the litter, leaping up in unseemly fashion kept trying to catch it.
sentences.i: But she could not hold out; when the beetle flew round the litter she sprang up, all decorum gone, and tried to catch it.
sentences.n: ἀκόσμως is the word the whole fable turns on: κόσμος is order and seemliness, and the leap breaks the decorum her new office requires. ἀντέχω is to hold out against a pressure. The imperfect ἐπειρᾶτο leaves the attempt still going on, and unfinished.

sentences.t: Καὶ ὁ Ζεὺς ἀγανακτήσας κατ’ αὐτῆς πάλιν αὐτὴν εἰς τὴν ἀρχαίαν τάξιν ἀποκατέστησεν.
sentences.tr: Kai ho Zeus aganaktēsas kat’ autēs palin autēn eis tēn archaian taxin apokatestēsen.
sentences.l: And Zeus, having grown angry at her, restored her again to her ancient station.
sentences.n: ἀγανακτέω κατά with the genitive is to be indignant against someone; the same phrase turns the ending of the fable of Momus (124) and of the tortoise (125). ἀποκαθίστημι is the formal word for putting a thing back where it belonged. τάξις is the rank or post assigned one.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι οἱ φαῦλοι τῶν ἀνθρώπων, κἂν τὰ προσχήματα λαμπρότερα ἀναλάβωσιν, τὴν γοῦν φύσιν οὐ μετατίθενται.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti hoi phauloi tōn anthrōpōn, kan ta proschēmata lamprotera analabōsin, tēn goun physin ou metatithentai.
sentences.l: The story shows that the base among men, even if they take on more brilliant appearances, do not at any rate change their nature.
sentences.n: κἄν is καὶ ἐάν run together by crasis, concessive with the subjunctive: 'even if'. πρόσχημα is what one holds out in front — the show presented to onlookers, which for the fox was the litter and the royal office. γοῦν concedes the show and refuses the substance.
